paper.title: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement

gap.author_gap: Existing language agents target a single app or terminal, and hand-crafting tools and prompts for the many OS applications is impractical; AutoGPT lacks self-directed learning of unfamiliar applications.
gap.checked_gap: Real limitation (fixed, human-designed tool set per application) but the specific change here, agent-generated tool library via practice, is the Voyager-style move ported to OS/Python tools; the paper states novelty mainly as integration.
gap.lineage: AutoGPT/OpenAgents multi-scenario agents -> Voyager-style self-directed skill learning (Minecraft) -> OS-level agent with generated Python tools; SheetCopilot as manually tooled spreadsheet specialist
gap.closest_adjacent: Voyager (named, not compared), AutoGPT, GPT-4 plugins, SheetCopilot; other tool-making agents are not discussed
gap.residue: Generalising to unfamiliar apps without per-app engineering
gap.stakes: Hundreds of OS applications cannot each get bespoke tools
gap.method_response: Retrieval-miss tool generation plus practice-time library growth with critic gating
gap.remaining_gap: Admission is judgment-based; no tool-level validation; benefit on GAIA is small and unreplicated; web/GUI apps unsupported
unresolved: Voyager and other skill-library agents are not in the pinned materials; novelty relative to them is not independently assessed.
